patients.summary: Retired postal clerk with severe COPD who joins in 2023 still smoking, quits in March 2025, and is found on screening CT that June to have extensive-stage small cell lung cancer. Chemo-immunotherapy course is complicated by a vomiting-related metabolic alkalosis, a right lower lobe pneumonia, and SIADH that brings her to the ICU with a sodium of 120 in March 2026.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

70F transferring care after many years at another primary care office in the valley; wanted a practice where she could reach the doctor directly.

COPD: told she had "severe" COPD about 9-10 yrs ago. Breathing tests at the old office, results not with her. Uses tiotropium HandiHaler every morning, Flovent Diskus 250 BID most days, albuterol a few times a week - more on humid days and walking up the hill to her mailbox. No ED visits or steroid bursts she can recall in the last 2 yrs. No home O2.

Tobacco: still smoking, about a pack a day, started late 20s. Over 40 pack-years. Has tried to stop twice, both times on her own. Not ready today - "I know, I know."

PMH: COPD. No surgeries.
Meds: tiotropium 18 mcg daily, fluticasone propionate 250 mcg BID, albuterol HFA PRN.
Allergies: NKDA.
FHx: father - lung cancer. Mother - emphysema. Brother - COPD.
SHx: retired from the post office (clerk at the counter for most of her career). Widowed. Lives alone in Leeds; daughter nearby. No alcohol. No drug use.

Exam: thin, pleasant, no distress at rest. Speaks in full sentences. Chest: diminished breath sounds throughout, prolonged expiration, no wheeze today, no crackles. Heart regular, no murmur. No clubbing. No edema.

A/P
1. COPD, reported severe - will get spirometry here next visit to document stage. Inhaler technique reviewed with the Diskus, decent. Continue current inhalers.
2. Tobacco use - advised to quit, plainly. Declines meds or the quitline for now; will keep asking.
3. Lung cancer screening - eligible by age and pack-years; LDCT ordered.
4. Records requested from prior office.
5. Return 3 wks for spirometry, labs.

documents.title: Prior Primary Care Records (fax)
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Records from prior primary care office, 23 pages, received by fax. Summary abstracted by MA:

- Problem list: COPD (severe); tobacco use.
- Meds on last visit (03/2023): Spiriva HandiHaler 18 mcg daily, Flovent Diskus 250 mcg 1 puff BID, ProAir HFA PRN.
- Colonoscopy 2018: normal, no polyps. Repeat not recommended before 10 yrs.
- Screening mammogram 2022: BI-RADS 1, negative.
- Immunizations on file: influenza 2021, 2022; COVID-19 mRNA primary series 2021 and a booster 2022. No pneumococcal or Tdap documented.
- Spirometry: referenced in a 2014 note as "severe obstruction"; the actual report is not included.
- Allergies: NKDA.

Scanned to chart. -MA

reports.text: Pre- and post-bronchodilator spirometry (albuterol 4 puffs). Acceptable and repeatable efforts, 3 trials. Post-bronchodilator FEV1 0.94 L (42% predicted). FEV1/FVC 0.52. No significant bronchodilator response. Flow-volume loop with a scooped expiratory limb.
reports.conclusion: Severe airflow obstruction, GOLD stage 3 (FEV1 30-49% predicted).

documents.title: COPD Follow-up with Spirometry
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Back for PFTs and labs. Breathing same as last visit. Still smoking a pack/day. Using tiotropium daily, Flovent most days - admits she skips the evening dose sometimes. Albuterol 3-4x/wk.

O: Vitals per flowsheet. Diminished BS, prolonged expiratory phase, no wheeze or crackles. Heart RRR. No edema.
Spirometry today: post-BD FEV1 0.94 L, 42% pred, ratio 0.52. No meaningful BD response.

A/P:
- COPD, GOLD 3 by today's numbers. Continue tiotropium, fluticasone, PRN albuterol. Encouraged twice-daily Flovent use and rinsing after.
- Tobacco: asked again, still declines treatment. Gave quitline card anyway.
- Labs today (CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH, hep C Ab).
- Tdap today, not on record.
- LDCT is scheduled next week.
- RTC 4-6 mo.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
INDICATION: Lung cancer screening, 70-year-old current smoker, over 40 pack-years. Baseline exam.
TECHNIQUE: Low-dose helical CT of the chest without IV contrast.
COMPARISON: None.
FINDINGS: Lungs: Centrilobular emphysema, upper lobe predominant. No pulmonary nodule. No consolidation. Airways patent. Pleura: No effusion or pneumothorax. Mediastinum and hila: No lymphadenopathy. Heart normal size. Upper abdomen: Unremarkable.
LUNG-RADS: Category 1, negative.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1. Emphysema. Continue annual screening with LDCT in 12 months.

documents.title: LDCT Lung Screening Result Note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: LDCT baseline: no nodules, Lung-RADS 1. Emphysema as expected with her COPD. Repeat in 1 yr. Message sent to pt.

documents.title: Your CT and blood work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Irene - your lung screening CT showed no spots or nodules. It does show emphysema, which is the CT picture of the COPD we already know about. We'll repeat the scan every summer as long as you're a smoker or recently quit.

Your blood counts, kidney and liver tests, thyroid and cholesterol were all fine, and the hepatitis C screen was negative.

And I'll keep saying it: the single best thing for your lungs is stopping cigarettes. Door's open whenever you want help.

documents.title: RE: Your CT and blood work
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you for letting me know so fast. Relieved. I hear you on the smoking.

reports.text: Bilateral screening mammogram with tomosynthesis. Comparison: outside 2022 exam reported negative (images not available). The breasts are almost entirely fatty. No suspicious mass, calcifications or architectural distortion. Skin and nipples unremarkable.

reports.text: Lumbar spine L1-L4 T-score -0.9. Left femoral neck T-score -0.8. Total left hip T-score -0.6. No prior for comparison.

- 2023-24 COVID (Pfizer), 0.3 mL IM R deltoid
- PCV20, 0.5 mL IM R deltoid (no prior pneumococcal on record)
Observed 15 min, tolerated well. Pt asked whether she needs the shingles shot - told her we'll plan that at her wellness visit in January.

documents.title: Medicare Annual Wellness Visit (Initial)
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
INITIAL AWV

Health risk assessment reviewed (completed in waiting room). Independent in ADLs and IADLs - drives, shops, keeps her own house. No falls in the past year; steady on Get Up and Go. Hearing and vision OK by self-report; sees an eye doctor every couple of years for readers. PHQ-2 = 0. No memory concerns from her or her daughter.

COPD stable since summer. Still smoking, "a bit less" - maybe 15/day. Counseled again; she'd like to try cutting down on her own first.

Prevention:
- Colon: colonoscopy 2018 normal, nothing due.
- Breast: mammo 8/2023 neg, repeat 2024.
- Bone: DXA 8/2023 normal.
- Lung: LDCT 7/2023 Lung-RADS 1, repeat 7/2024.
- Vaccines: flu, COVID, PCV20, Tdap all done. Shingrix #1 today, #2 in 2-6 mo.
- Hep C neg 2023.

Advance directives: none on file. Would want her daughter to speak for her. Gave the health care proxy form to take home.

Vitals per flowsheet, BMI about 23-24. Lungs diminished, no wheeze. Heart regular.

Plan: lipid panel today. Shingrix #2 nurse visit in March. COPD visit in spring.

documents.title: Shingrix #2
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Second Shingrix given 0.5 mL IM L deltoid. After dose 1 she had a sore arm and felt tired for a day, nothing else. Series complete.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Quit smoking on Saturday 3/1 as planned. Day 4. Irritable, "eating everything in the house," no cigarettes. Threw out the cartons. Breathing baseline. No cough change.

Tobacco: 45 pack-years by her count.

O: Vitals per flowsheet. Lungs diminished, no wheeze, no crackles. RRR.

A/P
1. Tobacco - quit 3/1/25. Big congratulations. Reviewed what to expect with cravings, offered patch for cravings - she wants to see how it goes without. Will check in by portal in 2 wks.
2. COPD GOLD 3 - stable. Continue inhalers.
3. LDCT still due in July - remains eligible (quit < 15 yrs).

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
INDICATION: Annual lung cancer screening. Former smoker, quit 03/2025, 45 pack-years.
TECHNIQUE: Low-dose CT chest without IV contrast.
COMPARISON: 07/23/2024, 07/19/2023.
FINDINGS:
There is a new 3.4 x 2.9 cm soft tissue mass in the right hilum, not present on the prior exam.
Enlarged right hilar and subcarinal lymph nodes, new since prior.
Centrilobular emphysema, upper lobe predominant, unchanged.
No pleural effusion. No pneumothorax. Heart size normal.
Visualized upper abdomen limited on this low-dose noncontrast exam.
LUNG-RADS: Category 4X.
reports.conclusion: New right hilar mass with right hilar and subcarinal adenopathy, Lung-RADS 4X, highly suspicious for malignancy. Recommend tissue sampling and PET-CT. Findings called to ordering provider at 12:35.

documents.title: Call - CT Result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Radiology called at 12:35 with today's screening CT: new right hilar mass ~3.4 cm with enlarged right hilar and subcarinal nodes, Lung-RADS 4X.

Called pt. Daughter was with her, on speaker with permission. Told them plainly this looks like it could be a lung cancer and that we need a biopsy to know. Pt quiet, then asked if it was because she smoked so long. Told her we don't need to go there right now; we need to get her seen quickly.

Urgent pulmonology referral placed, flagged for bronchoscopy. They'll likely want a PET. Our MA will call the pulm office tomorrow morning to push for a slot within 2 wks.

Offered a visit this week to talk through it; she'd rather wait until she sees pulm. Knows she can call or text me any time.

documents.title: Pulmonology Consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT PULMONARY CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 07/01/2025
Referred by: Primary Care Physician

Thank you for referring Ms. Whitney, a 72-year-old former smoker (45 pack-years, quit in March) with severe COPD, for a right hilar mass found on her annual screening CT of 06/10/2025.

She reports her breathing is at her usual baseline. Lung function: post-BD FEV1 0.94 L (42%) on your spirometry from 2023.

Medications: tiotropium 18 mcg daily, fluticasone propionate 250 mcg BID, albuterol PRN.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: father with lung cancer; mother emphysema; brother COPD.

Exam: thin woman in no distress. SpO2 on room air in the low-mid 90s. Diminished breath sounds bilaterally with prolonged expiration, no wheeze. No supraclavicular or cervical adenopathy. No clubbing.

Impression: New central right hilar mass with ipsilateral hilar and subcarinal adenopathy in a heavy former smoker - primary lung malignancy until proven otherwise; the central location raises small cell carcinoma among the possibilities.

Plan:
1. Flexible bronchoscopy with transbronchial biopsy of the right hilar lesion this week under moderate sedation; she understands the risks given her lung function.
2. PET-CT and MRI brain for staging, to be ordered once tissue is back.
3. Will copy you on results.

Pulmonology

conditions.label: Malignant neoplasm of lung
conditions.note: Small cell carcinoma, right hilar mass; biopsy 07/03/2025

reports.text:
SPECIMEN: Right hilar lesion, transbronchial biopsies (5 fragments).
GROSS: Multiple tan-pink tissue fragments, aggregate 0.6 cm, entirely submitted.
MICROSCOPIC: Sheets of small, round to oval cells with scant cytoplasm, finely granular chromatin, absent nucleoli and nuclear molding, with crush artifact and frequent mitoses. Background bronchial mucosa present.
IMMUNOHISTOCHEMISTRY: Tumor cells positive for TTF-1, synaptophysin and chromogranin; Ki-67 proliferation index approximately 90%.
reports.conclusion: Right hilar lesion, transbronchial biopsy: SMALL CELL CARCINOMA.

documents.title: Bronchoscopy Procedure Note
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
PROCEDURE: Flexible bronchoscopy with transbronchial biopsy, right hilar lesion.
DATE: 07/03/2025
INDICATION: Right hilar mass with hilar and subcarinal adenopathy.
SEDATION: Moderate sedation, monitored throughout.
FINDINGS: Normal vocal cords. Trachea and carina normal. No endobronchial lesion in either lung.
SAMPLES: Five transbronchial biopsies of the right hilar lesion under fluoroscopy; brushings and washings sent.
COMPLICATIONS: None. Minimal bleeding, settled with cold saline. Post-procedure chest film without pneumothorax.
DISPOSITION: Recovered and discharged home with her daughter.
Pathology to follow.

--- Addendum 07/07/2025: pathology shows small cell carcinoma. Patient informed by phone. Referred to medical oncology; staging PET-CT and MRI brain ordered.

documents.title: Call - Biopsy Result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Pulm called me ahead of the report - bronch biopsy is small cell carcinoma. They've told her and sent the oncology referral; PET and brain MRI ordered.

I called Irene after. She'd been crying but was clear-headed, daughter there. Explained small cell in simple terms: it tends to spread early, it's treated mainly with chemotherapy-type medicines, and it often responds well at first. We'll know more after the scans. Booked her with me 7/22 to go over things together. She thanked me for getting the CT done.

conditions.label: Secondary malignant neoplasm of right adrenal gland
conditions.note: 2.1 cm FDG-avid lesion on staging PET-CT; extensive-stage small cell lung cancer

documents.title: Staging Imaging (outside), reported to PCP
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Staging results forwarded by pulmonology, 07/14/2025 (formal reports not attached):

PET-CT skull base to mid-thigh, 07/10/2025: FDG-avid right hilar mass and FDG-avid right hilar and subcarinal lymph nodes, corresponding to the screening CT findings. 2.1 cm FDG-avid right adrenal nodule, consistent with metastasis. No other FDG-avid disease.

MRI brain with and without contrast, 07/10/2025: No intracranial metastasis. No acute abnormality.

Impression: extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (right adrenal metastasis). Medical oncology consult scheduled 07/17.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet (8 mg) by mouth every 8 hours as needed for nausea

documents.title: Medical Oncology Consultation
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
MEDICAL ONCOLOGY - NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Visit date: 07/17/2025

Diagnosis: Small cell lung cancer, extensive stage (right hilar primary, right hilar and subcarinal nodes, right adrenal metastasis). Biopsy 07/03/2025. MRI brain 07/10/2025 negative.

History: 72-year-old woman, former smoker of 45 pack-years who stopped in March 2025, with severe COPD (FEV1 42% predicted) on inhaled therapy. Mass found on screening CT. Breathing is at her baseline; she is up and about and caring for herself.

Meds: tiotropium, fluticasone propionate inhaler, albuterol PRN. Allergies: none known.

Exam: well-appearing. No adenopathy. Lungs with diminished air entry, no wheeze. Abdomen benign.

Labs today (CBC, CMP) within normal limits.

Assessment and plan:
Extensive-stage SCLC, good performance status. We discussed that treatment is not curative but aims to control disease and extend life with good quality, and that responses are common.
- Carboplatin AUC 5 day 1 plus etoposide 100 mg/m2 days 1-3 plus atezolizumab 1200 mg day 1, every 21 days for 4 cycles, then maintenance atezolizumab.
- Port placement by IR, requested for next week.
- Target C1D1 07/28/2025.
- Antiemetics: ondansetron 8 mg every 8 hours as needed sent to her pharmacy; standard premedications are given in the infusion center.
- Reviewed immunotherapy side effects, including thyroid, adrenal, lung and bowel inflammation; she will call for new cough, diarrhea, rash or fevers.
- Thank you for including us in her care. We will keep you updated.

Medical Oncology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Visit - New Diagnosis of Small Cell Lung Cancer
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with daughter. 50 min visit, mostly counseling.

Saw oncology on 7/17. Plan: port Thursday 7/24, then carboplatin/etoposide/atezolizumab starting 7/28, 4 cycles q3wk, then atezolizumab alone. They explained it's not curable but treatable. Has ondansetron at home.

How she's doing: worried, as anyone would be, but sleeping and eating. Not smoking - says the diagnosis made it easy. PHQ-9 = 3; denies hopelessness or SI. Knows the cancer center has a social worker if she wants one.

Breathing baseline. Exam: lungs diminished, no wheeze, no crackles. RRR. No edema.

Goals of care / ACP (~25 min): She wants full treatment. Daughter is HCP (form on file Jan 2025). We agreed to keep revisiting this as treatment goes on. Code status: full.

Plan:
- Oncology leads treatment; I'll keep her COPD, vaccines and everything else.
- Inhalers unchanged.
- Let me know about any fever over 100.4 - call oncology first, and me.
- RTC 2 mo or sooner.

documents.title: Oncology Same-Day Visit
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
MEDICAL ONCOLOGY - URGENT VISIT, 08/25/2025

Reason: vomiting since Friday 8/22, following C2 (08/18).

HPI: Nausea from day 3 of the cycle, then vomiting several times a day since Friday despite ondansetron. Little food and only sips of fluid. Lightheaded on standing. No abdominal pain, no diarrhea, no fever. No new cough beyond her usual.

Exam: tired, dry mucous membranes. Orthostatic - lightheaded with a drop in pressure on standing. Abdomen soft, nontender. Lungs diminished, no new findings.

Labs: Na 136, K 3.3, Cl 89, HCO3 34, BUN 30, Cr 1.2, glucose 104.

Assessment: Hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis due to vomiting, with volume depletion and mild hypokalemia, after cycle 2.

Plan:
- 2 L normal saline with 20 mEq KCl in the infusion center today; orthostatic symptoms resolved by the end of the infusion and she kept down crackers and ginger ale.
- KCl 20 mEq PO daily x 3 days.
- Continue ondansetron 8 mg q8h PRN; scheduled for the first 3 days of the next cycle.
- Repeat BMP in about a week - PCP office closer to home, patient will arrange.
- Call for recurrent vomiting.

Allergies: NKDA.
Medical Oncology

documents.title: Sick after chemo

documents.body: Good morning. I wanted you to know I was at the cancer center yesterday because I couldn't stop throwing up after the 2nd chemo. They gave me 2 bags of fluid and potassium pills for 3 days. My potassium and salts were off. They want blood work again next week and said I could get it at your office. I'm better today, ate toast.

documents.body: Thanks for telling me, Irene, I'm glad you're keeping things down. I put in the order for a chemistry panel - come by the lab any morning next week, Tuesday 9/2 works well. If the vomiting comes back or you get dizzy when you stand, call oncology right away.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
ED PHYSICIAN RECORD - copy released to PCP office on request
Arrival 09/08/2025 13:50; observation discharge 09/09/2025 11:20

CC: SOB, cough, fever.

HPI: 72 y/o F with severe COPD (GOLD 3) and extensive-stage small cell lung cancer on carboplatin/etoposide/atezolizumab (C2 08/18), right chest port. Three days of worsening breathlessness, yellow sputum, and fevers at home. No chest pain. No vomiting or diarrhea this time; was treated for vomiting and a metabolic alkalosis about two weeks ago at her cancer center. Former smoker, 45 pack-years, quit about 6 months ago.

Meds: tiotropium 18 mcg daily; fluticasone propionate 250 mcg BID; albuterol PRN; ondansetron 8 mg q8h PRN.
Allergies: NKDA.
FHx: father lung cancer, mother emphysema, brother COPD.
SHx: retired postal clerk, no alcohol.

Triage: T 38.6 C (101.5 F), BP 135/85, HR 102, RR 28.
Exam: tachypneic, speaking in short phrases. Crackles over the right lower lung field. No wheeze. Port site clean. No edema.

Results:
ABG on room air: pH 7.48, PaCO2 28, PaO2 60, HCO3 24.
CBC: no neutropenia.
CXR: right lower lobe infiltrate.

ED course: oncology fellow on call contacted - counts reassuring, OK to treat as CAP. Ceftriaxone 1 g IV and azithromycin 500 mg IV. Albuterol-ipratropium nebs x2. O2 2 L NC with improvement in work of breathing. Placed in observation overnight.

09/09: afebrile overnight, breathing easier, SpO2 92% on room air at rest and with ambulation in the hallway. Tolerating PO.

Diagnosis: Community-acquired pneumonia, right lower lobe. Acute respiratory alkalosis with hypoxemia on ABG, from pneumonia.

Discharge: amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg BID x 7 days; azithromycin 250 mg daily x 4 days. Continue inhalers. Oncology notified; they will decide on timing of C3. Follow up with PCP within 1 week. Return for worsening breathing, chest pain or confusion.

documents.title: Outside Fill Notification
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Med history feed shows two new fills today at her usual pharmacy from an ED prescriber: amoxicillin-clavulanate 875 mg BID #14 and azithromycin 250 mg #4. Nothing from the hospital received yet. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Call - ED Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Called pt after the fill notice. She was in the ED Mon 9/8 with fever and cough, told it was pneumonia in the right lung, kept overnight, sent home Tues on the 2 antibiotics. Today: no fever since Monday night, still coughing up yellow, breathing "better than Monday, not normal." Taking antibiotics. Oncology pushed chemo back a week.
Scheduled post-ED visit Fri 9/12 with PCP. Records request sent to the hospital ED. Reviewed return precautions.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u ED 9/8-9/9 for RLL pneumonia (record not yet received; history from pt and fill history).

S: Day 4 of amox-clav, finished azithro yesterday. No fever since Monday night. Cough less, sputum turning from yellow to white. Walking around the house without stopping. Appetite back. No vomiting since late August.

O: Vitals per flowsheet, afebrile. Comfortable, full sentences. Few crackles R base; no wheeze. RRR. Port site clean. No edema.

A/P
1. RLL CAP - clearly improving. Finish amox-clav through 9/15. Recheck if not back to baseline in 2 wks. Oncology to decide on restaging imaging, which will also show the RLL.
2. Extensive-stage SCLC - C3 rescheduled to 9/16.
3. COPD - inhalers unchanged, albuterol use back down.
4. Recent alkalosis from vomiting - resolved on 9/2 labs.
5. Flu/COVID shots in Oct, oncology OK with that between cycles.

documents.title: Fall Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Fall vaccines given a week after C4 (10/7), per oncology: high-dose flu L deltoid, 2025-26 COVID L deltoid (port is R chest). No fever today. Observed 15 min, no reaction. Pt says the cough from the pneumonia is gone and she's done with the 4 cycles; scan at the end of the month.

reports.text:
CT chest, abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast (restaging). Comparison: PET-CT 07/10/2025, LDCT 06/10/2025.
Right hilar mass now 1.9 cm (previously 3.4 cm). Right hilar and subcarinal lymph nodes decreased in size. Right adrenal nodule 1.2 cm (previously 2.1 cm). Right lower lobe airspace opacity seen on the September chest film has cleared. Centrilobular emphysema. No pleural effusion. Right chest port in place. No new lesion in the chest, abdomen or pelvis.

documents.title: Oncology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Dear Doctor,

I saw Ms. Whitney on 10/30/2025 after completing 4 cycles of carboplatin, etoposide and atezolizumab (last cycle 10/07; cycle 3 delayed one week for a right lower lobe pneumonia treated through the ED in September; vomiting with metabolic alkalosis after cycle 2, managed with IV fluids).

Restaging CT 10/28/2025 shows a partial response: right hilar mass 3.4 to 1.9 cm, adrenal lesion 2.1 to 1.2 cm, nodes smaller, nothing new. The right lower lobe opacity has cleared.

She is active and managing at home. Breathing is at baseline.

Plan: maintenance atezolizumab 1680 mg IV every 4 weeks starting 11/04/2025. Carboplatin and etoposide are complete. TSH and cortisol will be checked periodically on immunotherapy. Restaging CT about every 3 months.

Current meds: tiotropium, fluticasone propionate inhaler, albuterol PRN, ondansetron PRN. NKDA.

With thanks,
Medical Oncology

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: pulmonary and critical care
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY - Pulmonary & Critical Care Service
Admitted: 12/06/2025  Discharged: 12/10/2025

Principal diagnosis: Acute exacerbation of COPD with secondary bacterial pneumonia.
Secondary: Hyponatremia due to SIADH. Extensive-stage small cell lung cancer on maintenance atezolizumab. Severe COPD (GOLD 3).

History: 72-year-old woman, ED visit in September for a right lower lobe pneumonia, presented with three days of increasing breathlessness, cough productive of yellow sputum, and feeling weak all over. No fever, chest pain or travel.

On arrival: afebrile, BP 130/80, HR 88, RR 22, SpO2 92% on room air. Wheezing on both sides with crackles at the bases.

Data: Na 125, K 4.2, Cl 95, HCO3 24, BUN 18, Cr 0.9, glucose 98. Serum osmolality 260. Urine osmolality 500, urine Na 80.
Chest x-ray: increased interstitial markings, small right pleural effusion (not sampled).

Hospital course:
1. COPD exacerbation with bacterial pneumonia - ceftriaxone and azithromycin IV, scheduled albuterol-ipratropium nebulizers. Steady improvement; on room air throughout. Transitioned to oral amoxicillin-clavulanate.
2. Hyponatremia - hypotonic, euvolemic, concentrated urine with high urine sodium, normal renal function, in the setting of small cell lung cancer: SIADH. Fluid restriction 1.2 L/day. Sodium 125 -> 127 (12/8) -> 130 (12/10). No neurologic symptoms.
3. SCLC - oncology aware; next atezolizumab per their schedule.

Discharge medications:
- Albuterol HFA 2 puffs q4-6h PRN
- Fluticasone propionate 250 mcg 1 inhalation BID
- Ondansetron 8 mg q8h PRN nausea
- Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg BID x 3 more days
- Atezolizumab per oncology

Instructions: fluid restriction 1.2 L per day (about five cups total, including soups). PCP visit within one week with a chemistry panel. Return for confusion, worse breathing or fever.
Allergies: NKDA.
Condition at discharge: stable, ambulating, on room air.

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit. Admitted 12/6-12/10 (pulm/critical care service) for COPD exacerbation + pneumonia; new SIADH, Na 125 on admission, 130 at d/c. Discharge summary received 12/11 and reviewed. Our office called her 12/11 (within 2 business days).

S: Breathing nearly back to baseline. Last amox-clav dose tonight. Cough minimal. Doing the fluid restriction - measuring with a 1-quart pitcher plus a cup; finds it hard, thirsty in the evenings. No headache, no confusion, daughter agrees she's sharp.

Med rec: The hospital's discharge list leaves off tiotropium - she has been taking it every day and the inpatient team gave it to her; continue. Our list still had carboplatin/etoposide/atezolizumab 1200 from induction; updated - induction finished in October, now atezolizumab 1680 mg q4wk (letter 10/31).

O: Vitals per flowsheet, afebrile. Alert, oriented. Lungs: diminished, no wheeze, no crackles. RRR. No edema. Mucous membranes moist.

A/P
1. SIADH, from her small cell cancer most likely. BMP drawn today. Keep restriction 1.2 L/day. Tips: sugar-free hard candy, ice chips count, salty foods are fine. Recheck BMP early Jan.
2. COPD exacerbation/pneumonia - resolved clinically. Inhalers as before (tiotropium, fluticasone, PRN albuterol).
3. ES-SCLC - maintenance atezolizumab, next per oncology.
Return sooner for confusion, drowsiness, falls.

Addendum 14:10: Na 131. Called pt - stay the course.

reports.text: Noncontrast CT of the head. Indication: confusion, small cell lung cancer. No intracranial hemorrhage. No mass, mass effect or midline shift. No acute territorial infarct. Ventricles and sulci normal for age. Gray-white differentiation preserved. Visualized paranasal sinuses and mastoids clear.
reports.conclusion: No acute intracranial abnormality. No mass.

documents.title: ICU and Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: critical care medicine
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted via the ED to the medical ICU 03/07/2026; transferred to the floor 03/09; discharged home 03/12/2026.

Principal diagnosis: Severe symptomatic hyponatremia due to SIADH.
Other: Extensive-stage small cell lung cancer on maintenance atezolizumab. Severe COPD. SIADH first diagnosed 12/2025 (admission for COPD exacerbation and pneumonia).

Presentation: 73-year-old woman brought in by her daughter for two days of confusion and sleepiness. The daughter noticed her mother answering slowly and less engaged, and says she had been eating and drinking very little for about a week.

Exam: vital signs stable. Oriented to self only - not to place or date. Mucous membranes moist, no orthostatic findings, no sign of dehydration. Non-focal neurological exam.

Data: serum Na 120, serum osmolality 260, urine Na 45, urine osmolality 500. CT head: no acute abnormality, no mass. TSH 1.8, AM cortisol 14.2 (adrenal and thyroid causes excluded, relevant on immunotherapy).

Course: ICU admission for symptomatic hyponatremia. 3% saline with sodium checks every 2-4 hours; correction limited to no more than 8 mEq/L in 24 hours. Na 120 -> 125 at 24 h -> 128 (3/10) -> 130 (3/12). Mentation back to baseline by 3/9, transferred to the floor. Low solute intake over the preceding week likely contributed on top of SIADH. Oncology consulted; continue atezolizumab on schedule.

Discharge medications:
- NEW: sodium chloride 1 g tablet PO three times daily with meals
- Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily
- Fluticasone propionate 250 mcg inhaled BID
- Albuterol HFA PRN
- Ondansetron 8 mg PO q8h PRN
- Atezolizumab per oncology

Instructions: fluid restriction 1 L per day. Eat regular meals with salt. BMP within one week with PCP. Return for confusion, drowsiness, falls or seizure.
Allergies: NKDA.
Condition at discharge: alert and oriented x3, ambulating independently.

reports.text: CT chest, abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast. Comparison 01/20/2026 and 10/28/2025. Treated right hilar mass and right hilar and subcarinal nodes stable compared with January. Right adrenal nodule stable. No new pulmonary nodule, effusion or new lesion in the chest, abdomen or pelvis. Centrilobular emphysema. Right chest port in place.

documents.title: Oncology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Dear Doctor,

Follow-up for Ms. Whitney, extensive-stage small cell lung cancer on maintenance atezolizumab 1680 mg every 4 weeks since 11/04/2025.

Interval: admitted 03/07-03/12 with symptomatic hyponatremia from SIADH (Na 120), corrected slowly with hypertonic saline; now on sodium chloride tablets and a fluid restriction, with Na 133 on your 04/13 labs - thank you for following this closely. TSH and AM cortisol were normal during the admission.

Restaging CT 04/17/2026 shows the response maintained, with nothing new; January's scan was also stable.

She looks well today. Plan: continue maintenance atezolizumab, next restaging in about 3 months. Please continue managing the sodium; we are happy to discuss if it falls again.

Medications reviewed: tiotropium, fluticasone propionate, albuterol PRN, ondansetron PRN, sodium chloride 1 g TID. NKDA.

Medical Oncology
